title: Die yield and chip cost
summary: Real dies by area, the defect models that give their yield, and what yield does to the cost of silicon and to chip design (chiplets).

concepts.label: Die
concepts.description: One chip cut from a wafer; logic chips and image sensors here.

children.label: Process node
children.description: The fabrication process (Wikidata P2079), often missing.

children.label: Chiplet
children.description: A smaller die that, with others, makes one chip in a package.

concepts.label: Wafer
concepts.description: A 300 mm silicon disc processed as a unit; its cost is roughly fixed per node.

children.label: Defect density
children.description: Killer defects per cm² (D0); scenarios 0.05–0.5 here, not measured data.

children.label: Wafer cost
children.description: Price of a processed wafer; with dies per wafer and yield it sets cost per die.

concepts.label: Yield model
concepts.description: The share of dies without a killer defect as a function of area and D0.

children.label: Murphy yield
children.description: Y = ((1 − e^(−AD0))/(AD0))²: defect density varying across wafers (Murphy 1964).

children.label: Negative binomial yield
children.description: Y = (1 + AD0/α)^−α: clustered defects (Stapper); α the cluster parameter.

concepts.label: Cost per good die
concepts.description: Wafer cost / (dies per wafer × yield); here per good mm² relative to an ideal die.
